findings.where: Hero heading: the name line "MARK · M · MOSELEY" and the role line "INFRASTRUCTURE · ADVISOR", at desktop and phone
findings.fault: The name and the role are set in the same red Cinzel capitals, at the same size, weight and tracking. Nothing marks one line as the name and the other as what he does. On desktop the role line is longer, so it is the wider and stronger line and outweighs the name. On phone the role breaks over two lines, so the heading reads as one three-line block of equal capitals.
findings.who_objects: Mark, and the bank staff he wants to reach. The brief says the individual is the brand, yet his name gets no more weight than a generic job title. A visitor's eye lands on 'INFRASTRUCTURE' first, not on 'MOSELEY'.

findings.where: Article specimen: the post title "THE WORLD'S BEST PUBLIC-PRIVATE PARTNERSHIP LAW", and the related-link title "Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the 'Abundance' Challenge" below it
findings.fault: Article titles are set in Cinzel, which has capitals only. A seven-word title already takes three lines of solid capitals, and Mark's real titles run longer: the 'Streamlining…' title would take four or five lines of all-caps that read slowly. In the same specimen the related article's title is in bold sentence-case sans, so one kind of text, an article title, is set two different ways.
findings.who_objects: A reader at a development bank scanning Mark's articles, who reads long titles fastest in mixed case. Also Angélique, who will paste in real, long titles and get a block of capitals the tile never showed.

findings.where: Article specimen: the dateline "MMM INFRA BLOG NO. 8 · 18 SEPTEMBER 2024" against the related item's "Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF"
findings.fault: The two datelines in the specimen are set differently. One is in tracked Cinzel capitals, the other in plain Alegreya Sans. The Cinzel one also breaks the tile's own type rule (Cinzel is for 'headings, the nav and the button only'). On phone the tracked capitals wrap, leaving '2024' alone on a line.
findings.who_objects: Angélique and whoever builds the next round, who need one rule for metadata. Readers see two styles for the same kind of information.

findings.where: Motion sketch notes: 'cubic-bezier(0.5, 0, 0.2, 1)' and 'docs/research/animation-length.md' in the running text, at desktop and phone
findings.fault: These two strings drop into the browser's default monospace inside the small Alegreya Sans notes. That is a fourth typeface, larger and heavier than the text around it, so it breaks the line's colour and rhythm. It is also the default font stack the guardrails rule out.
findings.who_objects: The founder judging the tile as the site's type system: a default-stack face appears that the type pair never names.
